name: Synth string section: 7-voice unison saw, subtle bow-brightness envelope, LFO-on-detune vibrato with ramped rate, low FM blend
goal: Build a light cinematic string section from saws: 7-voice unison saw (~7% detune) into a low-resonance 12/6 dB low-pass ~400–450 Hz with a little drive, slow amp envelope (A ~1.5 s, D ~5 s, S ~70%, R ~2 s, full velocity), a subtle filter envelope (+15% range) for bowing brightness, ensemble vibrato by LFO-modulating unison detune (1 s, small amount) whose rate is swept by a second ramp LFO, a second 7-voice osc FM'd by the first at ~30–35%, then low-cut, gentle top cut, big reverb, quiet quarter-note delay, and 20–30% soft clip on macros.

source.title: How To Make A Cinematic String Section - Sound Design Tutorial

prerequisites: Synth with ≥2 oscillators, unison with detune, osc FM from another osc, filter with drive, 2 envelopes, 2 LFOs with LFO→LFO-rate routing, FX (EQ, reverb, delay, distortion), macros

inputs.name: attack_s
inputs.description: Amp attack; 1.5 s default, 2–4 s for slow swells, short for immediate

outputs.name: string_section_patch
outputs.description: Lightweight cinematic string-section patch with ensemble vibrato and macro FX control

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Recreate from the parameter relationships; do not load or copy the vendor-bundled preset of the same name.

Delta vs evolving-pad-unison-filter-swell-fifth and chorus-ensemble-classic-vibrato-pad-modes: vibrato comes from LFO on unison detune with an LFO-swept rate plus osc-to-osc FM blend, aimed at orchestral strings rather than pads or chorus FX.

steps.action: Init patch. Osc1 saw, 7 unison voices, ~7% detune; set the two osc start controls the video zeroes (unnamed in the transcript; typically phase/random-phase) to 0 to avoid clicks and pops. Route through filter 1: analog low-pass 12 dB/oct (6 dB works even better), resonance 0, cutoff ~450 Hz (later ~400 Hz), a little drive.
Amp envelope: attack ~1.5 s, decay ~5 s, sustain ~70%, release ~2 s. Velocity sensitivity 100%; polyphony ~24 voices so notes don't cut each other off.
steps.expect: Swelling strings that respond to playing dynamics

steps.action: Bowing brightness: envelope 2 attack ~0.5–0.6 s (rounded curve), decay ~4–5 s, sustain ~20–30%, release ~0.1 s → filter cutoff with a small amount (~15). Keep it subtle.
steps.expect: Slight brightening at note start, then settles

steps.action: Ensemble vibrato: LFO1 at 1 s period → unison detune amount ~0.06 (detune moves roughly 7% → 10–11% and back) rather than modulating global pitch.
steps.expect: Many-players vibrato shimmer, pitch centre stable

steps.action: Variable vibrato speed: LFO2 as a ramp, 4–5 s period → LFO1 rate (amount ~0.2) via the mod matrix so vibrato starts slow and speeds up, then resets.
steps.expect: Vibrato speed changes over the held note

steps.action: Second osc: 7 unison voices ~10% detune through filter 1, FM from osc1 at a low amount (~30–35%; high amounts sound bad).
steps.expect: Saws blend into a more orchestral timbre

steps.action: FX: low-cut rumble (keep lows only for bass use), take a little off the top to reduce fizz, reverb with high mix and large size (decay up to 4–5 s), quarter-note mono delay with low feedback and low mix, soft-clip distortion with drive up and mix ~20–30% (end of chain, or before reverb so the reverb carries the grit).
steps.expect: Glued, spacious strings with optional grit

steps.action: Macros: one macro → distortion drive, one → reverb mix, and one macro to several FX at once (reverb + delay) for quick performance control.
steps.expect: Single macro moves multiple FX coherently

verification: Holding a chord shows audible slow-to-fast vibrato change over ~4–5 s
Bypassing the FM osc makes the patch sound more like a plain electronic pad
Amp attack change (short vs 2–4 s) clearly changes the onset
